title: How to celebrate festivals with children in need · AquaTerra
description: How AquaTerra has marked Christmas, Durga Puja, Diwali, Holi and Rakhi with children, one craft and one story at a time. {count} festival drives since {firstYear}.
lede: Festivals give a reason to gather children, and AquaTerra has written up {count} festival drives since {firstYear}, about half of them at Pather Sathi's Sunday School. Christmas comes up most often, then Durga Puja, Diwali, Rakhi and Holi, and most of the sessions were craft days with a song, a story or a treat added on top.

sections.heading: start with the festival the children know
body: Christmas runs through this page more than any other festival. The Merry Miracles series ran as a string of days in December 2023, mostly at Pather Sathi's Sunday School, and came back in December 2024 and December 2025. Each year used a different craft, game or song, which gave the series a shape a new team can copy.

Durga Puja followed a similar path. Colours of Durga was a run of workshops at the Sunday School in September and October 2023, and Festive Spirit, a Durga Puja workshop run alongside Sujata Child NGO, ran that October too. Disco Diwali is different: it is the fundraising night, and it ran at New Alipore in October 2024 and at Chowringhee Banquets in October 2025.

sections.heading: where the festival happens
body: About half the festival drives on this page were at Pather Sathi. Ek Tara and AIM Foundation hosted a few more, and Disha Foundation, Ektara, Tetultala Ashram and Calcutta Rescue each hosted a Christmas drive. A place that children already come to every week is the easiest place to hold a festival.

The nights that pay for this work sit beside the drives. The Starry Night, a Christmas carnival fundraiser, ran at Sky Turf in December 2024 and again in December 2025. Each night is a separate event with its own name and date, and the drives are the part the children take home.

sections.heading: make something the children take home
body: Most festival drives were craft days. Children made Christmas greeting cards, paper masks and wrapping paper, and the Rakhi sessions had them making rakhis to tie. Merry Miracles Day 1 in December 2025 had kids making Christmas cards, and the Santa mask session at AIM Foundation in December 2025 had three kids make Santa masks with volunteers.

Add one song or one story to the craft. The Christmas carol sessions at Pather Sathi's Sunday School in December 2023 taught classic tunes, and Christmas Carols and Storytelling in December 2025 ended with cake and classic festive stories. Secret Cheer at Tetultala Ashram in December 2024 had children make wrapping paper, then wrap gifts for a Secret Santa game later in the day.

sections.heading: come back each year
body: Festival drives that come back are the easiest to plan. Merry Miracles returned in three Decembers, and the Rakhi workshops ran in August 2023, 2024 and 2025, each at a different place: South Calcutta Inner Wheel School, Ek Tara and BSS school.

Keep the joy simple. The Green Christmas drive at Ek Tara in December 2021 asked volunteers to swap plastic for plants, crafts and conscious cheer. The clearest drives on this page had one festival, one craft and one story, and that is a good shape to copy.

learnings: Christmas drives repeated in the same places each year, so a team can reuse a format that already worked.
Crafts were the most common activity, and a card, a mask or a rakhi gives the children something to take away.
The festival drive and the fundraising night are separate: the night pays for the welfare work, and the drive is what the children take part in.
Rakhi came back in three different years, so a team that runs one can plan the next.

faqs.q: How can I celebrate a festival with children who need it?
faqs.a: Choose one festival, one craft and one story, and hold it at a place where children already gather, such as a Sunday school. AquaTerra has run {count} festival drives since {firstYear}, and about half of them were at Pather Sathi's Sunday School.

faqs.q: What did AquaTerra do for Christmas with children in 2024?
faqs.a: In 2024 AquaTerra ran {year:2024} festival drives on this page, and several were Christmas drives. They included Merry Miracles quiz and letter writing at Pather Sathi, a Christmas carnival workshop there, a Secret Santa session at Tetultala Ashram and a Christmas fete at Calcutta Rescue.

faqs.q: Does AquaTerra run Durga Puja drives for children?
faqs.a: Yes. The Colours of Durga workshops ran at Pather Sathi's Sunday School in September and October 2023, and a Durga Puja workshop run alongside Sujata Child NGO took place that October too.

faqs.q: Is Disco Diwali a drive for children?
faqs.a: No. Disco Diwali is AquaTerra's Diwali fundraising night, and it helps pay for the welfare drives. The most recent one, The Masquerade Sangeet Edition, was held on 10 November 2026 at Chowringhee Banquets.

faqs.q: Where can I help celebrate a festival with children in Kolkata?
faqs.a: Most festival drives have been at Pather Sathi, with Ek Tara, AIM Foundation and a few schools hosting others. To help at the next one, join AquaTerra through the join page.
